q-340853.name: Question 1
q-340853.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=3{x}^{2}+2x$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ The Fourier series of the $4$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
q-340853.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=2$ and $f(x)=3{x}^{2}+2x$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(3{x}^{2}+2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}]}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(({2}^{3}+{2}^{2})-((-2)^{3}+(-2)^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(12-(-4)) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $F(x)=7x+\pi $ for $x\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}).$ The Fourier series of the $\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
q-341806.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $f(x)=7x+\pi $ for $x\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(7x+\pi )\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+\pi x]}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }((\frac{7}{2}\cdot \frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2})-(\frac{7}{2}\cdot \frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}-\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2})) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }({\pi }^{2}) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

q-341856.name: Question 4
q-341856.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=3x+1$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ The Fourier series of the $4$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${b}_{4}.$

${b}_{4}=$ {{field-1}}
q-341856.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the sine coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=2$ and $f(x)=3x+1$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(3x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{2}x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(3x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x+1\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{1}{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}(uv\,{|}_{-2}^{2}-{\int }_{-2}^{2}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2\pi }[(3x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)]_{-2}^{2}+\frac{3}{2\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2\pi }((3(2)+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\pi )-(3(-2)+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(-4\pi ))+\frac{3}{2\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{2\pi }{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)]}_{-2}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2\pi }(7\cdot 1-(-5)\cdot 1)+\frac{3}{4{\pi }^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-4\pi ))) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{12}{2\pi }) \\  & =-\frac{3}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Let $F(x)=5x$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ The Fourier series of the $4$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${b}_{3}.$

${b}_{3}=$ {{field-1}}
q-353158.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the sine coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=2$ and $f(x)=5x$ for $x\in (-2,2).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{b}_{3}=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(5x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}x)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{2}{3\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}x)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(uv\,{|}_{-2}^{2}-{\int }_{-2}^{2}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{2}{3\pi }{[5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}x)]}_{-2}^{2}+\frac{10}{3\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\pi }(-{[5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}x)]}_{-2}^{2}+5{\int }_{-2}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\pi }(-(5(2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\pi )-5(-2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(-3\pi ))+\frac{10}{3\pi }{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}x)]}_{-2}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\pi }(20+\frac{10}{3\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3\pi ))) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\pi }\cdot 20 \\  & =\frac{20}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
